title: voids: chained runs with accumulation
purpose: Exercises the accumulation branch of `voids` [@epsrmanual]: each run reads the histograms of the previous runs and forms a running average over `nsumt` configurations, and the random-number sequence used to sample the void-pixel correlation continues from the state saved in `randomno.dat`, as in a real multi-configuration analysis.
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Pixels within 2.2 Å of the listed atom types are marked (`include S O`, DMSO sulphur and oxygen only; with an `include` list occupied and unoccupied pixels are swapped), connected regions are labelled and their size histogram and pixel-pixel correlation are computed; random origins come from the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992]. The reference `fort.14` gives a pixel fraction of 0.35069.
inputs: `chain.VOIDS.n01` and `randomno.dat` were produced by one Fortran run of the same input with `nsumt 0`; the input `chain.VOIDS.dat` (`nsize 80`, `npix 100`, radius 2.2 Å, `include S O`) was then set to `nsumt 99`. `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test.
verification: `repeat 2`: each pass reads the previous histograms (running average with nsum = 100) and continues the random sequence from `randomno.dat`. Because `voids` writes nsumt into the `npix` entry, nsumt itself stays 99 and npix becomes 100, so every pass starts from the same pixel grid and the chain remains valid (reference `.dat`: `npix 100`, `nsumt 99`). Compared after each pass: `chain.VOIDS.n01`, `chain.VOIDS.dat`, `fort.14`, `randomno.dat`. The configuration is the same in every pass, so the chained passes test the read-back of the accumulated file and the running-average arithmetic.
